claims.text: Greater atomic-size mismatch among HEA constituents induces local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions caused by atomic-size mismatch disrupt optimal electron-phonon coupling.
Greater atomic-size mismatch lowers the superconducting transition temperature.
Greater atomic-size mismatch alters superconducting-gap characteristics.
Low-mismatch, simple-structure HEAs exhibiting conventional BCS-type superconductivity are an available baseline system.
Varying the proportions of elements with substantially different atomic radii can deliberately increase atomic-size mismatch while leaving overall electronic composition similar.
Atomic-size mismatch generates local strain and lattice distortions.
Local strain and lattice distortions disrupt regular phonon modes.
Regular phonon modes are essential for strong electron-phonon coupling in the proposed HEAs.
Disruption of phonon modes weakens electron-phonon coupling and Cooper-pair formation.
Weaker Cooper-pair formation produces a lower transition temperature.
High-mismatch samples should have a lower Tc than low-mismatch baseline samples.
High-mismatch samples should show a reduced gap magnitude or modified gap structure in tunneling spectroscopy.
Low-mismatch HEAs have been shown to possess conventional BCS s-wave superconductivity with optimal lattice symmetry and electron-phonon coupling.
Carrier-concentration changes can independently affect Tc and therefore confound the mismatch comparison.
Extremely large atomic-size mismatch may produce secondary phases or additional scattering mechanisms that complicate interpretation.
Prior evidence indicates that lattice distortions can influence Tc in conventional superconductors.
The magnitude of the Tc and gap shifts may depend on elemental selection and the degree of mismatch.
